question: What is the medical term for guinea worm disease?
explanation: Dracunculiasis is the scientific name given to the condition caused by the Guinea worm parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h1)

question: Why does a guinea worm outbreak heavily impact the economy of a rural farming community?

options.A: Government quarantine rules restrict export of local farm produce
options.B: High mortality rates drastically reduce the available workforce
options.C: Prolonged physical incapacitation prevents agricultural labor during peak seasons
options.D: Expensive pharmaceutical treatments bankrupt local health clinics

explanation: The disease causes long-term disability rather than death, stopping farmers from working their fields when it matters most. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h1)

question: Which organism serves as the intermediate host for Dracunculus medinensis?
explanation: Microscopic water fleas ingest the parasite larvae and act as the necessary intermediate host in stagnant water sources. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h2)

question: How do the parasite larvae gain entry into the human body?

options.A: Direct penetration of unbroken skin while wading in flooded rice fields
options.B: Bites from infected blood-sucking aquatic insects near riverbanks
options.C: Inhalation of airborne dust particles near drying ponds during harmattan
options.D: Ingestion of contaminated drinking water containing infected water fleas

explanation: Infection occurs exclusively through swallowing water that holds copepods carrying the parasite. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h2)

question: What triggers the female guinea worm to release its larvae into the environment?

options.B: Contact of the skin blister with surface water
options.C: Elevation in the host's internal core body temperature
options.D: Exposure of the patient to direct sunlight

explanation: The adult worm responds to water immersion by forcefully ejecting larvae to infect waiting water fleas. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h3)

question: A patient with a broken guinea worm blister wades into a village drinking pond. What is the direct public health consequence?

options.A: The pond water gains a foul chemical taste that repels other villagers
options.B: The surrounding soil absorbs the larvae and becomes infertile for crops
options.C: The water source becomes heavily contaminated with thousands of parasite larvae
options.D: Fish in the pond consume the worms and become poisonous to humans

explanation: Wading introduces massive numbers of larvae into the communal drinking supply, perpetuating the transmission cycle. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h3)

question: Which symptom typically precedes the physical emergence of the adult guinea worm?

options.A: Profuse watery diarrhea and electrolyte collapse
options.B: Intense burning pain and blister formation at the site
options.C: Persistent dry cough and pleural chest pain
options.D: Sudden paralysis of both lower extremities

explanation: Patients experience a severe, localized burning sensation and a blister right before the worm breaks through the skin. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h4)

question: Why do some patients develop generalized hives and low-grade fever prior to worm emergence?

options.A: Side effects of traditional herbal concoctions ingested for pain
options.B: Bacterial invasion through tiny microscopic skin abrasions
options.C: Dehydration caused by working under the hot tropical sun
options.D: Allergic reactions to metabolic toxins released by the maturing parasite

explanation: The body mounts an immune response against antigens and secretions produced by the living worm just underneath the skin. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h4)

question: What is the primary method used to diagnose guinea worm disease?

options.A: Urinalysis using chemical reagent strips for nematode antigens
options.B: Microscopic analysis of a fasting morning blood serum sample
options.C: Stool microscopy for detection of parasite ova and cysts
options.D: Visual inspection of the characteristic blister and protruding worm

explanation: The physical appearance of the worm emerging from a skin ulcer provides an immediate and definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h5)

question: When assessing a patient with a confirmed guinea worm lesion, what should the nurse prioritize checking?

options.A: Neurological reflexes in the upper extremities
options.B: Liver enlargement and elevated serum bilirubin levels
options.C: Signs of secondary bacterial infection and cellulitis around the ulcer
options.D: Visual acuity and potential retinal detachment from larval migration

explanation: The open skin lesion creates an entry point for bacteria, making secondary wound infections a common and dangerous complication. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h5)

question: What is the main danger of forcefully pulling out a guinea worm too quickly?

options.A: The skin will develop permanent hyperpigmented keloid scars
options.B: The worm may snap, causing severe inflammation and secondary infection
options.C: The patient will instantly lose consciousness from neurogenic shock
options.D: The parasite will immediately migrate upward into the cerebral cortex

explanation: Rupturing the worm leaves dead tissue inside the body, provoking a severe immune reaction and heavy bacterial contamination. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which pharmacological intervention forms the cornerstone of clinical treatment for guinea worm disease?

options.A: Symptomatic pain relief and wound dressings, as no specific curative drug exists
options.B: Daily oral doses of specialized larvicides to dissolve the adult parasite
options.C: Intravenous administration of broad-spectrum systemic anti-helminthics
options.D: Prophylactic corticosteroids to completely suppress local immune reactions

explanation: Because drugs do not kill or cure the worm, treatment relies entirely on supportive care and mechanical extraction. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h6)

question: Which severe and potentially fatal bacterial infection is strongly associated with guinea worm wounds?
explanation: The necrotic wound track creates a low-oxygen environment where tetanus spores can easily germinate and produce toxins. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h7)

question: Why might a patient develop a permanent joint contracture following a guinea worm infection?

options.A: Direct destruction of articular cartilage by migrating micro-larvae
options.B: Severe systemic calcium depletion caused by the parasite feeding on bone
options.C: Calcification of muscle tissue surrounding the dead male worms
options.D: Prolonged joint immobilization in a flexed position to relieve intense pain

explanation: Holding a joint bent for weeks to ease pain can lead to permanent shortening of tendons and muscles around the joint. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h7)

question: What is a simple, low-cost method taught to villagers to prevent guinea worm infection from drinking water?

options.A: Adding powdered table salt to storage pots
options.B: Filtering water through clean cloth or fine mesh
options.C: Exposing water buckets to direct afternoon sunlight
options.D: Stirring water vigorously with fresh neem tree branches

explanation: Simple cloth filters effectively trap the microscopic water fleas carrying the infective parasite larvae. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of case containment strategies implemented by community health nurses?

options.A: To ensure patients take a full course of expensive oral antibiotics
options.B: To force mandatory quarantine of entire villages in government isolation camps
options.C: To stop infected persons from contaminating shared water sources and spreading larvae
options.D: To gather biological specimens for laboratory parasite gene sequencing

explanation: Containing a case ensures that the emerging worm never comes into contact with community drinking water, breaking the transmission chain. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h8)
